references.text: Describes the counting of seven weeks from the day the sheaf was brought forward, which is the basis for the Feast of Weeks mentioned in Deuteronomy 16:9.
Mentions the Feast of Weeks (Shavuot) and the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, which are directly linked to the counting of seven weeks.
Refers to the day of the week when the firstfruits of the wheat are brought forward, marking the end of the seven weeks that are counted.
Describes the beginning of the harvest and the bringing forward of the sheaf, which is the starting point for the counting of the seven weeks.
Pentecost (Greek: Pentekoste) is the fiftieth day after the counting of seven weeks, and is the New Testament fulfillment of the Feast of Weeks.
Paul wished to be in Jerusalem by Pentecost, which is the feast celebrated after the counting of the seven weeks.
